subject: Clarifying billing rounding, aggregation windows, and anti-abuse floors
messages:
From: Samara Patel <samara@brightdocs.com>
To: irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Robert Liu <robert.liu@brightdocs.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Billing mechanics question — rounding, long-context, and anti-abuse floors

Irene — thanks for the demo yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from our finance and infra teams around how Redwood will actually bill some of our traffic patterns. We're trying to model monthly spend and want a clear, conservative approach for procurement. Short list of asks (we attached a couple of sample payloads):

1) Rounding / quantum: If a single API call consumes 3 prompt tokens and returns 12 generated tokens, how will that be rounded? Do you aggregate across rapid calls from the same conversation?

2) Long-context behavior: We often pass a 180k-token corpus (split client-side) as context to a single request. How do you bucket or split huge contexts for billing? Any per-chunk minimums?

3) Anti-abuse / streaming floors: Our product will do lots of short streaming lookups (few tokens each) in high frequency. Are there minimum charges per streamed session or per-minute smoothing thresholds we should model?

4) Examples: Could you provide worked examples for three scenarios (single short call, many small streams within a minute, and one very large context request)?

We attached sample_payloads.json and a small spreadsheet with a sample usage profile. Also, we have an outstanding SOW draft — would like to align billing language there. Can you loop in someone from engineering and sales to make sure we've captured limitations?

Thanks —
Samara Patel
Head of Platform, BrightDocs
Samara.p@brightdocs.com

Attachments: sample_payloads.json (json), billing-sample-calcs.xlsx (xlsx)
From: irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Samara Patel <samara@brightdocs.com>
Cc: Robert Liu <robert.liu@brightdocs.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing mechanics question — rounding, long-context, and anti-abuse floors

Samara — appreciate the concrete examples, that helps. Looping in Aditya (billing/runtime) and Marissa (sales) to give concrete calculations and a commercial suggestion. High level answers up-front, then Aditya will follow with math: 

- Quantum/rounding: Redwood counts prompt + generated tokens per request, then aggregates across an "aggregation window" when requests are part of the same logical conversation (by conversation_id or same session token). We use a 60-second aggregation window by default for that grouping. After aggregation we apply an 8-token billing quantum (round up to nearest 8 tokens) to reduce invoice noise for very small bursts.

- Long-context: Very long contexts are sharded into 8k-token context buckets at the serving layer. Billing counts the active buckets referenced in the request; partial buckets round up to full 8k chunks. For >64k contexts we also consider them multi-bucket and apply per-bucket quantization.

- Streaming / anti-abuse: There is a streaming floor to prevent abuse from micro streams — by default short streaming sessions that total <16 tokens in a 60s window are billed a minimum of 16 tokens. However for pilot customers we can consider waiving that floor for a defined period (details below).

Aditya — could you put together worked examples using Samara's sample_payloads.json? Marissa — we should propose a pilot concession (waive streaming floor for 3 months and a small discount on bucket charges) and add language to the SOW.

Next steps: Aditya will send the worked calculations; Marissa will draft a SOW clause and a pilot concession. If useful, Samara — we can book a 30-min call to walk through numbers.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Senior Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com

Attachment: None
From: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>, Samara Patel <samara@brightdocs.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Jun 2028 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing mechanics question — rounding, long-context, and anti-abuse floors

Hi all — below are worked examples using the policy Irene summarized. I used the sample payloads spreadsheet columns (prompt_tokens, gen_tokens, session_id, total_context_tokens). All calculations show the billed tokens after aggregation and quantum/flooring; final billed units are what appear on the invoice.

Scenario A — single short call (single request, unique session_id)
- prompt_tokens = 3, generated_tokens = 12
- raw tokens = 15
- aggregation window: no other requests in 60s -> aggregated tokens = 15
- quantum = 8 tokens -> round up to nearest 8 = 16 billed tokens
- billed on invoice: 16 tokens

Scenario B — many small streams in tight window (10 micro-streams over 45s, same session_id)
- each stream: prompt 2, gen 3 -> per-stream 5 tokens; 10 streams = raw 50 tokens
- aggregation: same session within 60s -> aggregated = 50 tokens
- quantum 8 -> round up to nearest 8 = 56 billed tokens
- streaming floor doesn't apply because aggregated total > 16 (floor only hits when aggregated < 16)
- billed on invoice: 56 tokens

Scenario C — very large context (client split into parts, server-referenced)
- total_context_tokens passed = 180,000 tokens (client-side split into 23 chunks of ~7826 tokens)
- serving sharding: bucket size = 8,192 tokens (8k nominal); 180,000 / 8,192 = 21.97 -> rounds up = 22 buckets charged
- per-bucket accounting: request also generates 2,000 tokens; total billed = (22 * 8,192) + 2,000 = 180,224 billed tokens -> in practice we report billed tokens as 180,224
- note: we also present a compressed "context-bucket" line item on invoices so customers can reconcile buckets vs token totals

Edge cases / notes:
- If a customer intentionally issues many tiny requests across different session_ids, aggregation won't combine them; the 60s aggregation is per-session_id.
- We can change aggregation window and quantum at contract time for enterprise/Dedicated customers (e.g., 30s window or 4-token quantum), but that requires a commitment tier and is written into the SOW.
- Streaming floor waiver: for a short commercial pilot we can set the streaming floor to 0 for the agreed period; after the pilot the default 16-token floor will reapply unless SOW says otherwise.

I've attached a small sheet with these line-item calculations (billing-sample-calcs.xlsx). Happy to walk through any of the numbers on a call.

- Aditya Rao
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com

Attachment: billing-sample-calcs.xlsx (xlsx)
From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samara Patel <samara@brightdocs.com>
Cc: irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jun 2028 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing mechanics question — rounding, long-context, and anti-abuse floors

Samara — thanks for the clear ask and thanks Aditya for the examples. We discussed commercially and propose the following pilot terms we can include in the SOW draft (attached SOW-draft.pdf):

1) Pilot period: 3 months from activation.
2) Streaming floor: waived for pilot customers for the duration (streaming floor = 0).
3) Context bucket discount: 10% off billed context-bucket charges for any bucketized context calls during pilot.
4) Aggregation/quantum: keep default 60s aggregation window and 8-token quantum for hosted product; for Dedicated we can negotiate a 4-token quantum as part of capacity commitment.
5) Reconciliation: Redwood will provide a per-day CSV export of raw token counts and billed tokens for reconciliation during the pilot.

Action items:
- Samara: confirm acceptance of pilot terms and any required PO/SOW edits.
- Irene: I'll update the SOW and include the pilot concession lines and a clause that describes the aggregation window and bucket-size (so procurement can sign off).
- Aditya: please confirm the CSV export format (daily) and include a sample.

If that sounds good, I can send a redline of the SOW this afternoon. If BrightDocs needs a longer pilot or a custom quantum, we can price that as an addendum.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
